boys.hpp / boys.cpp — Boys Function

On this page

  • Overview

  • Functions

  • Example

Overview

Efficient, numerically stable computation of the Boys function \(F_n(x)\) required by the McMurchie-Davidson integral engine.

Header: include/boys.hpp Source: src/boys.cpp

For the mathematical definition and derivation of the three evaluation regimes see Boys Function.

Functions

double boys_F(int n, double x)
Parameters:

  • n – Order \(n \ge 0\).

  • x – Argument \(x \ge 0\).

Returns:

\(F_n(x) = \int_0^1 t^{2n} e^{-xt^2}\,dt\).

Convenience wrapper that allocates a temporary vector of size \(n+1\), calls boys_Fvec(), and returns the last element. Prefer boys_Fvec() in hot loops.

void boys_Fvec(int nmax, double x, double *F)
Parameters:

  • nmax – Maximum order; computes \(F_0, F_1, \ldots, F_{n_\text{max}}\).

  • x – Argument \(x \ge 0\).

  • F – Output array of size at least \(n_\text{max}+1\) (caller-allocated). F[n] receives \(F_n(x)\).

Fills all Boys values in a single pass. This is the primary entry point used by the integral engine, which requests \(n_\text{max} = \ell_1+\ell_2+\ell_3+\ell_4\) per primitive quartet.

The three evaluation strategies used internally:

Range

Method

\(x \le 10^{-14}\)

Trivial limit: \(F_n = 1/(2n+1)\).

\(0 < x < 1\)

Taylor series \(\sum_{k\ge 0} (-x)^k / [k!\,(2n+2k+1)]\) (converges in < 30 terms).

\(x \ge 1\)

\(F_0 = \tfrac{\sqrt\pi}{2\sqrt{x}}\operatorname{erf}(\sqrt{x})\), then upward recurrence \(F_{n+1} = [(2n+1)F_n - e^{-x}]/(2x)\); asymptotic fallback if result is non-finite.

Example

#include "boys.hpp"

// Single value
double f2 = boys_F(2, 3.5);   // F_2(3.5)

// Full vector (preferred in integral loops)
int nmax = 4;
double F[5];
boys_Fvec(nmax, 1.23, F);
// F[0] = F_0(1.23), ..., F[4] = F_4(1.23)
